<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
          <jats:p>
            Thiosulfate dehydrogenase is known to play a significant role in thiosulfate oxidation in the acidophilic, obligately chemolithoautotroph,
            <jats:named-content content-type="genus-species">Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans</jats:named-content>
            . Enzyme activity measured using ferricyanide as the electron acceptor was detected in cell extracts of
            <jats:named-content content-type="genus-species">A. ferrooxidans</jats:named-content>
            ATCC 23270 grown on tetrathionate or sulfur, but no activity was detected in ferrous iron-grown cells. The enzyme was enriched 63-fold from cell extracts of tetrathionate-grown cells. Maximum enzyme activity (13.8 U mg
            <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
            ) was observed at pH 2.5 and 70°C. The end product of the enzyme reaction was tetrathionate. The enzyme reduced neither ubiquinone nor horse heart cytochrome
            <jats:italic>c</jats:italic>
            , which serves as an electron acceptor. A major protein with a molecular mass of ∼25 kDa was detected in the partially purified preparation. Heme was not detected in the preparation, according to the results of spectroscopic analysis and heme staining. The open reading frame of AFE_0042 was identified by BLAST by using the N-terminal amino acid sequence of the protein. The gene was found within a region that was previously noted for sulfur metabolism-related gene clustering. The recombinant protein produced in
            <jats:named-content content-type="genus-species">Escherichia coli</jats:named-content>
            had a molecular mass of ∼25 kDa and showed thiosulfate dehydrogenase activity, with maximum enzyme activity (6.5 U mg
            <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
            ) observed at pH 2.5 and 50°C.
          </jats:p>
title: Tetrathionate-Forming Thiosulfate Dehydrogenase from the Acidophilic, Chemolithoautotrophic Bacterium Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
          <jats:p>
            <jats:named-content xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" content-type="genus-species" xlink:type="simple">Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans</jats:named-content>
            is a major participant in consortia of microorganisms used for bioleaching. It can obtain energy from the oxidation of Fe
            <jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>
            , H
            <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
            , S
            <jats:sup>0</jats:sup>
            , and various reduced inorganic sulfur compounds (RISCs). Tetrathionate is a key intermediate during RISC oxidation, hydrolyzed by tetrathionate hydrolase (TetH), and used as sole energy source. In this study, a
            <jats:italic>tetH</jats:italic>
            knockout (Δ
            <jats:italic>tetH</jats:italic>
            ) mutant and a
            <jats:italic>tetH</jats:italic>
            overexpression strain were constructed and characterized. The
            <jats:italic>tetH</jats:italic>
            overexpression strain grew better on sulfur and tetrathionate and possessed a higher rate of tetrathionate utilization and TetH activity than the wild type. However, its cell yields on tetrathionate were much lower than those on sulfur. The Δ
            <jats:italic>tetH</jats:italic>
            mutant could not grow on tetrathionate but could proliferate on sulfur with a lower cell yield than the wild type's, which indicated that tetrathionate hydrolysis is mediated only by TetH, encoded by
            <jats:italic>tetH</jats:italic>
            . The Δ
            <jats:italic>tetH</jats:italic>
            mutant could survive in ferrous medium with an Fe
            <jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>
            oxidation rate similar to that of the wild type. For the
            <jats:italic>tetH</jats:italic>
            overexpression strain, the rate was relatively higher than that of the wild type. The reverse transcription-quantitative PCR (qRT-PCR) results showed that
            <jats:italic>tetH</jats:italic>
            and
            <jats:italic>doxD2</jats:italic>
            acted synergistically, and
            <jats:italic>doxD2</jats:italic>
            was considered important in thiosulfate metabolism. Of the two
            <jats:italic>sqr</jats:italic>
            genes, AFE_0267 seemed to play as important a role in sulfide oxidation as AFE_1792. This study not only provides a substantial basis for studying the function of the
            <jats:italic>tetH</jats:italic>
            gene but also may serve as a model to clarify other candidate genes involved in sulfur oxidation in this organism.
          </jats:p>
title: Construction and Characterization of tetH Overexpression and Knockout Strains of Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans
